title: Input to the `knowledge.proposeChange` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `knowledge.proposeChange`, the content write-intent tool (ADR-0032 decision 1). SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2). The tool maps 1:1 onto `ProposalService.draft`: it writes a proposal directory a human reviews and merges, and reaches no approved-state write (ADR-0013).

**The body is inline text, and there is no path, URI, or reference field anywhere in this input (ADR-0032 decision 2).** This is a structural security property, not a refusal a handler makes: the daemon runs as the operator, so a body path would be a read primitive over the operator's filesystem — private keys, `~/.claude.json`, anything the operator can read — laundered into a proposal directory and, by ADR-0013 point 7, into a pull request. An absent parameter has nothing to be got right about symlinks, case folding, Unicode normalisation or TOCTOU on.

**Composition.** The context every project-scoped call carries — `projectId`, and the optional `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` — arrives by `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json` rather than being restated here. The closure is `unevaluatedProperties: false` and not `additionalProperties: false`, which under a `$ref` composition rejects the very context fields it referenced (ADR-0031 decision 1). `projectId` is required by the referent and is not repeated in this file's `required`.

**Evidence is authoritative, and requiredness is preserved over the wire (ADR-0032 decision 4).** `evidence.agentId` and `evidence.taskId` are required and are what reach the proposal's evidence record; the top-level tool-context `agentId`/`taskId` remain optional ambient provenance and are never read into a proposal. When a top-level field is present and disagrees with its evidence counterpart, the call is refused in the handler — a cross-field equality between a `$ref`'d context property and a nested one is a constraint a schema states only awkwardly.

**`body` carries a `maxLength` in code points; the transport cap is bytes.** The whole request body is rejected above `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` at the transport (`daemon/server.py`, #669). This field-level `maxLength` counts code points while that cap counts bytes, and the unit is recorded rather than re-litigated at [#691](https://github.com/theurian/theurian/issues/691); it is a sound over-approximation of the byte cap that no admitted request can exceed.

**What this file constrains, and what it leaves to the handler.** Shape, length and the closed `contentType` set. The other vocabularies (`kind`, `trustLevel`, `sensitivity`) stay handler refusals with a remedy that names the valid values, and the identifier grammar of `itemId` and `expectedRevision` stays a handler refusal too, for the reason `knowledge-search-input.schema.json` records.

itemId.description: The knowledge id the proposal is for, e.g. architecture.retry-policy. At most 200 characters, which is `MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH` — the bound `ItemId` itself enforces. A well-formed id this caller may not read and one that was never stored are the same answer (SEC-13, ADR-0032 decision 6): a refusal about an out-of-view item carries no current-revision id and no status.

title.description: Human title for the revision. Refused empty by the handler.

kind.description: What sort of knowledge, e.g. architecture, decision, security. The closed set is `KnowledgeKind`; an unknown value is refused by the handler with a remedy naming the valid kinds, rather than answered here with `does not satisfy`.

owner.description: Team that owns this knowledge. Refused empty by the handler.

author.description: The human who will own the change. Refused empty by the handler.

description.description: Why the change is being made. Refused empty by the handler.

body.description: The revision body, as inline text (ADR-0032 decision 2 — never a path, URI, or reference). At most `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` code points; the transport rejects a larger request in bytes first (#669), and the code-point/byte unit is #691.

contentType.description: The media type of `body`. A closed enum (ADR-0032 decision 1): the CLI derives it from a filename suffix, and there is no file on this path, so the caller states the type instead.

evidence.description: Where the proposed change came from and why (ADR-0013 point 5). Provenance only: Theurian does not authenticate agents. This object is authoritative for `agentId` and `taskId` (ADR-0032 decision 4).

agentId.description: Which agent drafted this. Required, and what reaches the evidence record.

taskId.description: The unit of work it came out of. Required.

model.description: The model identity that produced it. Required.

reasoning.description: Why the evidence supports the claim. Required — a proposal with no reasoning is rejected at generation.

sourceAnchors.description: Where this knowledge came from (FR-R5, INV-8). One wire field fills both the reviewed evidence record and the migration's own `metadata.sourceAnchors`. A revision needs at least one anchor, or the `authored-in-theurian` label; the handler refuses a request that has neither.

provider.description: Anchor provider, e.g. git or github.

repository.description: Repository the anchor names, if any.

commitSha.description: Commit the anchor pins, if any.

filePath.description: File the anchor names, if any.

labels.description: Free-form labels to group this knowledge by. `uniqueItems` because the migration's `revisionMetadata.labels` is `uniqueItems`, so a duplicate is refused at the wire with a key path rather than as a validation failure over a document the caller cannot see (ADR-0032 decision 3). Pass `authored-in-theurian` to declare the knowledge originates here and carries no external source.

scopePaths.description: Globs this knowledge governs, e.g. src/**. The order is kept.

namespace.description: Namespace to record. Absent defaults to the item id's own.

trustLevel.description: How much scrutiny this content has had. Absent means "not stated" — never a stamped default, which would assert a judgement the caller did not make (#249). The closed set is `TrustLevel`; an unknown value is a handler refusal.

sensitivity.description: Disclosure class. Absent means "not stated", never a stamped default. The closed set is `Sensitivity`; an unknown value is a handler refusal.

expectedRevision.description: The current revision id of an existing item (ADR-0006 optimistic concurrency). Required for an update and refused on a first revision — the handler derives which from the caller's own view of the approved set (ADR-0032 decision 6).

local.description: Draft under .theurian/proposals-local/ instead (ADR-0028). Defaults to false. A parameter of the act, not a field of the reviewed text.
